::: {.lede}
When we go to hospital, we expect to leave healthier than when we arrived. But what if the place we go to recover can also expose us to another health risk?
:::

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="64%"}
Healthcare-associated infections (HAIs) are infections that patients pick up during medical care, such as infections of surgical wounds, the urinary tract or the lungs. They vary in type and severity, and they can increase the risk of illness, death and healthcare costs. Anyone who goes to hospital, including us or someone close to us, could be affected. 
:::

::: {.column width="6%"}
:::

::: {.column width="30%"}
![](purple_nurse.jpg){fig-alt="A nurse in purple scrubs"}
:::

::::

A 2019 study estimated that Germany had around 478,000 cases of five common HAIs, causing about 16,000 deaths. These numbers sound alarming, but they do not tell us what to expect as a patient. This raises a question:

::: {.finding}
**How likely are you to catch an infection in a German hospital, and how serious is it, compared with the rest of Europe?**
:::

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(plotly)
```

```{r}
# Dataset 1: Germany by infection type (for the table)
hai_types <- data.frame(
  type   = c("UTI", "HAP", "SSI", "CDI", "BSI"),
  cases  = c(214150, 106586, 93222, 36002, 26976),
  deaths = c(3664, 3968, 2328, 1917, 3905)
)

hai_types$pct_death <- round(hai_types$deaths / hai_types$cases * 100, 1)

# Sort from most to least common
hai_types <- hai_types[order(-hai_types$cases), ]

# Add the paper's reported totals as the last row (not the sum of the rows)
hai_types <- rbind(
  hai_types,
  data.frame(type = "Total", cases = 478222, deaths = 16245,
             pct_death = round(16245 / 478222 * 100, 1))
)


# Dataset 2: Germany vs EU/EEA (for the bar chart)
# Source: Table 2, Zacher et al. (2019). DALYs per 100,000 population.
# Samples used: "German PPS" and "ECDC PPS (EU/EEA)".
hai_compare <- data.frame(
  type    = rep(c("HAP", "UTI", "BSI",
                  "SSI", "CDI"), times = 2),
  region  = rep(c("Germany", "EU/EEA average"), each = 5),
  dalys = c(86.1, 82.6, 72.2, 35.7, 25.9,       # Germany
                109.8, 57.1, 76.2, 35.1, 10.0),     # EU/EEA
  lower  = c(42.1, 34.5, 38.3, 28.9, 2.5,           # Germany, lower limit
             55.3, 24.3, 52.6, 33.3, 0.9),          # EU/EEA, lower limit
  upper  = c(145.1, 159.2, 129.0, 43.7, 61.2,       # Germany, upper limit
             170.5, 102.9, 104.8, 36.8, 19.2)       # EU/EEA, upper limit
)

# Keep the infection types in this order on the chart
hai_compare$type   <- factor(hai_compare$type,
                             levels = c("HAP", "UTI", "BSI",
                             "SSI", "CDI"))
hai_compare$region <- factor(hai_compare$region,
                             levels = c("Germany", "EU/EEA average"))
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-type
#| tbl-cap: Estimated yearly hospital infections and deaths in Germany, 2011, by type of infection.
kable(
  hai_types,
  col.names = c("Type of infection", "Infections per year",
                "Deaths per year", "Share leading to death (%)"),
  format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
  align = "lrrr"
) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) |>
  row_spec(0, background = "#674A7D", color = "white") |>
  row_spec(c(1, 3, 5), background = "#E8E3F5") |> 
  row_spec(nrow(hai_types), background = "#E8E3F5", color = "#333333", bold = TRUE)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-hai
#| fig-cap: Healthy years of life lost per 100,000 people by type of hospital infection, Germany compared with the EU/EEA average, 2011-2012.
hai_plot <- hai_compare |>
  ggplot(aes(x = type, y = dalys, fill = region,
  text = paste0(region, "<br>", type, ": ", dalys,
                           " (range ", lower, "-", upper, ")"))) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.8), width = 0.7) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
    position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
    width = 0.2, colour = "#555555"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Germany" = "#A98FBF",
                               "EU/EEA average" = "#F2B880")) +
  labs(
    x = "Type of infection",
    y = "Healthy years lost per 100,000 people",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

ggplotly(hai_plot, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(margin = list(l = 80, b = 80, t = 30, r = 20),
  legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.1))
```
